strengths: Clear and intuitive core motivation: Using raw 4D motion sequences instead of 2D rendered poses avoids information loss and pixel-level copying artifacts
Strong empirical results on TikTok benchmark: FID-VID of 6.98 substantially outperforms second-best (20.64), with consistent improvements across multiple metrics
Comprehensive experimental validation including thorough ablation studies on key components (motion tokenizer, motion attention, CFG) and systematic codebook analysis
Solid technical execution combining VQVAE tokenization with motion-aware DiT and well-motivated 4D RoPE positional encodings
Good generalization demonstrated across diverse styles (anime, photorealism, pixel art) and character types in qualitative results
Thoughtful dataset curation with multi-stage filtering pipeline to ensure high-quality training data
Good reproducibility with code and supplementary materials provided and clear implementation details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Primarily combines existing techniques (standard VQVAE, DiT, cross-attention); 4D RoPE is straightforward dimensional extension; motion tokenization via VQVAE is established practice
Very small evaluation benchmark (only 6 TikTok test videos) is insufficient for reliable generalization assessment; single-benchmark evaluation is a major limitation for top-tier venues
Overstated 'open-world' generalization claims contradicted by acknowledged limitations (fails on extreme body proportions, insufficient hand control, cannot support multi-person with different poses)

Evaluation methodology concerns: No user studies despite subjective animation quality; some baselines use numbers from original papers (potential inconsistent evaluation settings); no statistical significance testing or computational cost comparison

Technical justification gaps: Using dataset-wide mean joint positions for 4D RoPE spatial coordinates lacks principled justification; how distribution shift affects different body sizes unclear; distinction from 2D rendering in terms of pixel-level copying not rigorously explained

Limited ablation studies: CFG shows minimal impact on FID-VID yet is used in final model (robustness concern); no comparison with 2D pose rendering using same MV-DiT; no ablation on dataset filtering thresholds; missing comparison to reference network approach
Training data limitations: Only 5K pairs after 83% rejection rate; predominantly single-person dance motion; generalization to other motion types and multi-person scenarios unclear

Incomplete analysis: Only two failure cases shown; no systematic study of when/why method outperforms alternatives; limited motion complexity analysis; inconsistency in baseline results (MimicMotion and second-best both report 20.64)
Reproducibility gaps: Hyperparameter choices (codebook size, code dimension, L1 vs MSE loss) lack justification; some design decisions appear ad-hoc; SMPL estimation error propagation not analyzed
Ethical concerns briefly acknowledged but not thoroughly addressed; only planned safeguards mentioned, not implemented

strengths: Clear and well-motivated core contribution: direct 4D motion tokenization provides more expressive spatial-temporal guidance than 2D-rendered poses, with convincing intuition and empirical validation

Comprehensive technical system design with thoughtful engineering: differential joint coordinates, rigorous dataset curation, novel 4D RoPE extensions, and motion-aware guidance are all well-justified
Strong experimental results: achieves SOTA on TikTok and Fashion benchmarks with consistent improvements across multiple metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FID, FVD)
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 2-4) validating each component, demonstrating necessity of discrete quantization, differential motion, 4D MA, and 4D RoPE
Impressive zero-shot generalization to unseen motions, diverse character styles, and non-human subjects (animals, objects), demonstrating practical versatility
Scalability demonstration from 6B to 18B parameters with clear performance improvements, valuable for practical deployment

Extensive supplementary materials with detailed analysis: codebook efficiency analysis (Figure 8), reconstruction on unseen data (Figure 9), 4D RoPE visualization (Figure 10), and comprehensive implementation details
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty in individual components: diffusion transformers, RoPE, VQVAE are established; 4D RoPE extension is relatively incremental; novelty lies primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation
Missing critical user studies: quantitative metrics (FVD, LPIPS) don't capture perceptual animation quality, controllability, or user preferences—essential for character animation evaluation

Dataset diversity and quality concerns: filtering from 200K to 30K videos raises selection bias questions; limited documentation of demographic diversity (body types, ethnicities, ages); single-person extraction limitation not thoroughly addressed
Insufficient computational analysis: no inference time, memory requirements, or efficiency comparisons provided; computational costs critical for practical deployment
Limited failure case analysis: only hand control issues shown (Figure 7); systematic failure mode analysis and boundary conditions needed for comprehensive evaluation

Superficial ethical considerations: brief ethics statement; potential for misuse (deepfakes, identity manipulation) acknowledged but no concrete safeguards, content filtering, or watermarking discussed

Incomplete technical justifications: why discrete tokens outperform continuous representations (Appendix E analysis is limited); 4D RoPE design lacks deeper theoretical grounding; trade-offs between quantization loss and modeling benefits underexplored

Dataset curation process underspecified: quality assessment thresholds, filtering criteria, and motion uncertainty filtering (top 10% discarded) appear ad-hoc without exploring alternatives or sensitivity analysis

Generalization claims potentially overstated: 'unprecedented zero-shot generalization' needs more careful qualification; comparisons with recent generalist models limited; demonstrations mostly show motion transfer rather than novel motion generation
Limited analysis of learned motion semantics: no visualization of what motion tokens learn, no exploration of motion token space interpolation or reusability across characters
